fields.statement: Rhiza's own bug workflows serve m4-orchestrated-by-rhiza: they take the owner out of planning and shipping a bug, as recent fixes to Rhiza's own runs serve milestone 4's intents
fields.wording: (assumed by the planner in an autonomous run, no owner to ask)

fields.statement: The note on how bug requests flow in this repo goes in CLAUDE.md, not docs/: docs/runs-and-daemon.md and docs/custom-workflows.md already explain dispatch for every repo, and this note is about Rhiza's own repo only
fields.wording: (assumed by the planner in an autonomous run, no owner to ask)

fields.acceptance: rhiza workflow check plan-bug and rhiza workflow check bugfix pass (a warning about autonomous runs with bypassed permissions is expected), rhiza workflow describe plan-bug and bugfix each show the repo layer and autonomous, rhiza workflow ls lists both from .rhiza/workflows, and make self-check passes
fields.statement: This repo dispatches bug requests to autonomous workflows: .rhiza/dispatch.toml sets [request] bug = "plan-bug" and [ready] bug = "bugfix" with no schedules, .rhiza/workflows/plan-bug.toml wraps the built-in plan and .rhiza/workflows/bugfix.toml wraps the built-in ship-change, each as one workflow step with autonomous = true, so a bug is planned and shipped with no owner step whatever rhiza.autonomy.* says; there is no GitHub intake script, no rhiza.eventCommand hook and no issue label

fields.acceptance: CLAUDE.md names rhiza request --kind bug, .rhiza/dispatch.toml, plan-bug and bugfix, says both run autonomous with no owner step and that bugs do not come from GitHub issues; every command it names exists (rhiza request --help, rhiza workflow describe plan-bug and bugfix succeed)
fields.statement: CLAUDE.md has a short section on how a bug reaches and moves through this repo: queued as rhiza request --kind bug (CLI, the Request app, the orchestrator, the watchdog), planned by plan-bug and shipped by bugfix with no owner step, and never from GitHub issues
